hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Frequent Vehicle Access Points
hazards.description: Multiple garage doors and wide curb cuts on the left side create numerous conflict points where vehicles may cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street along the brick buildings

hazards.name: Degraded Roadway Surface
hazards.description: The asphalt shows signs of cracking and patching, which can create uneven surfaces for pedestrians crossing the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway area

hazards.name: Sidewalk Degradation
hazards.description: Cracks and vegetation growth in the sidewalk surface create potential tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side foreground and mid-ground

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no designated, protected walkway for pedestrians, forcing them into the street or parking areas.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire foreground and midground along the building frontage

hazards.name: Vehicle Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the paved apron block potential walking paths and create blind spots for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right side of the image in front of the garage doors

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: Multiple garage entrances and a continuous curb cut mean vehicles frequently cross the pedestrian path without clear demarcation.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire building frontage

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb block visibility between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Crossings
hazards.description: Multiple wide curb cuts for industrial access on the left create numerous conflict points for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Separation
hazards.description: There is no designated walkway, requiring pedestrians to walk in the vehicle travel and maneuvering area.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire foreground and midground area

hazards.name: Vehicle Maneuvering Conflict
hazards.description: The presence of multiple garage doors indicates frequent vehicle backing maneuvers into the shared pedestrian space.
hazards.location_in_image: Center background at garage doors

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are placed within the narrow sidewalk area, forcing pedestrians to maneuver around them.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Uneven and Degraded Surfaces
hazards.description: The unpaved areas adjacent to the road are uneven and contain debris, creating tripping hazards for those attempting to walk off the main pavement.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center-right edges of the paved roadway

hazards.name: Narrow walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalks are very narrow, providing little room for pedestrians to pass each other or for those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left and right sides

hazards.name: Poor pavement quality
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven road surface may present tripping hazards or cause vehicle swerving.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground roadway

hazards.name: Parked vehicles on walkway
hazards.description: Multiple vehicles are parked across the entire width of the paved walkway, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center-left foreground

hazards.name: Industrial equipment obstruction
hazards.description: A cement mixer and other equipment are stored on the sidewalk area, creating further blockages for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side in front of the brick building

hazards.name: Lack of vertical separation
hazards.description: There is no raised curb or physical barrier separating the roadway from the pedestrian area, increasing the risk of vehicle encroachment.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the edge of the asphalt roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both sides of the street obscure sight lines between pedestrians (especially children) and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb on both sides of the roadway

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Large vehicles, such as the silver pickup truck, can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side foreground

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A large driveway opening under the building crosses the sidewalk, creating a point where vehicles and pedestrians may collide.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, under the brick building

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parking
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block sightlines between the sidewalk and the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom right and left foreground

hazards.name: Parked vehicle sightline obstruction
hazards.description: A parked vehicle on the right side of the frame may obstruct the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalks
hazards.description: The sidewalks are relatively narrow and lack a buffer from the street, which may feel uncomfortable for pedestrians when vehicles are passing.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, adjacent to the white and brick row houses.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is situated in the center of the sidewalk, reducing the effective walking width and creating a barrier for those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground on the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a safe path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at intersections or mid-block to provide designated crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions near intersections or potential crossing points to improve visibility for pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install vertical traffic calming measures to ensure low vehicle speeds on this residential street.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Installing street trees or planters would provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the street while improving the microclimate.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Adding dedicated pedestrian lighting would improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install raised, paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide physical separation between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a buffer between the roadway and the new sidewalk, while also improving the aesthetic and environmental quality of the street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, paved sidewalk with a curb to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians at night.

interventions.title: Site Clearance and Maintenance
interventions.description: Remove debris and tires from the public right-of-way and enforce parking regulations to keep the pedestrian path clear.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a planting buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide physical separation and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Install speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential environment.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological barrier from traffic.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential context.

interventions.title: Install Raised Sidewalk
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant raised sidewalk with a distinct curb to separate pedestrians from the roadway and parking areas.

interventions.title: Curb Management and Parking Enforcement
interventions.description: Define specific parking zones and use bollards or curbs to prevent vehicles from encroaching on the pedestrian walkway.

interventions.title: Designated Pedestrian Path
interventions.description: Install a clearly marked or physically separated walkway to provide a safe space for pedestrians away from vehicle maneuvers.

interventions.title: Shared Space Signage
interventions.description: Install signage to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians and indicate pedestrian priority in this shared environment.

interventions.title: Improved Lighting
interventions.description: Install wall-mounted or pole-mounted lighting to improve visibility for pedestrians and drivers during low-light conditions.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove overgrown shrubs that obstruct sightlines at property entrances and along the roadway edge.

interventions.title: Raised Sidewalk and Curbing
interventions.description: Install a standard raised sidewalk with a vertical curb to clearly define the pedestrian zone and prevent vehicle parking on the walkway.

interventions.title: Parking Management and Enforcement
interventions.description: Designate on-street parking spaces and implement enforcement to ensure the walkway remains clear of vehicles and equipment.

interventions.title: Pavement Repair
interventions.description: Repair cracked and uneven concrete surfaces to eliminate trip hazards and improve accessibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars before they cross.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Vegetation
interventions.description: Adding street trees would provide shade, improve the aesthetic of the residential block, and act as a psychological traffic calming measure to slow vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Daylighting)
interventions.description: Implementing curb extensions at the ends of the block would improve visibility by preventing parking too close to intersections and shortening the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Incorporate a planting strip or furniture zone to provide physical and psychological separation between pedestrians and traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Driveway Treatment
interventions.description: Use contrasting pavement materials or bold paint markings across the driveway to signal pedestrian priority to drivers.

interventions.title: Parking Setbacks (Daylighting)
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the driveway to improve visibility for exiting drivers and approaching pedestrians.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Adding street trees would provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and vehicles while improving the streetscape.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening or Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate the utility pole or widen the sidewalk to ensure a minimum clear path of at least 4 feet for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to increase separation from traffic.
